What are Barcodes?

Barcodes are machine-readable visual symbols composed of parallel bars and spaces of varying widths. They encode numbers, alphanumeric characters, or symbols to allow optical scanners to instantly identify items. Barcoding is the international standard for automating inventory management, tracking packages, and speeding up retail point-of-sale checkout processes.

Supported Industry Barcode Standards

Tooleefy's generator supports the most common industrial and retail symbologies:

  • Code 128: A high-density, versatile alphanumeric barcode standard used globally in shipping, supply chain tracking, and container labeling.
  • EAN-13: The international 13-digit retail barcode standard required on consumer goods outside of North America.
  • UPC: The universal 12-digit product symbology widely used for retail products across the United States and Canada.

Guidelines for Printing and Scanning Barcodes

To prevent warehouse scanner read failures, adhere to these industrial standards:

  • Always output barcodes in solid high-contrast black ink on a non-reflective white background.
  • Ensure you respect the minimum required bar height and spacing specifications for your target symbology.
  • Maintain safe 'quiet zones' on the left and right sides of the bars so laser scanners can detect the boundaries.
  • Print using high-quality thermal label printers to avoid ink bleeding or gaps.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Which barcode format should I use for shipping boxes?

Code 128 is the absolute standard for shipping containers and logistics labeling due to its compact width and support for letters, numbers, and symbols.

Do I need a paid license to generate these barcodes?

No, our generator is completely free. However, if you plan to sell products in retail stores, you must register unique barcode numbers officially through GS1.

How can I download my barcodes in bulk?

Use the bulk generator tab, paste your list or upload a CSV file, and click generate. Our local engine will download them all as a single organized ZIP folder.
